working: |adj A| = |A|^(n-1) for an n x n matrix. So 3^(n-1) = 243 = 3^5, giving n-1 = 5, n = 6.

Matrix multiplication is associative wherever the products are defined. If AB and BC both exist then A(BC) and (AB)C are both defined and equal. It is not unconditionally true, because the factors must be conformable, so 'Always true' is wrong.
A is 3x2 and B is 2x3, so AB is 3x3. For an n x n matrix M, |kM| = k^n |M|; with n = 3, |kAB| = k^3 |AB|.
notes: Question-design flaw (not an option-labelling defect): since rank(AB) <= 2 < 3, |AB| = 0 necessarily, so all four options evaluate to 0 and are numerically indistinguishable. The intended answer via |kM| = k^n|M| with n = 3 is unambiguously C, so the key should read C; flagging only because the question is degenerate as posed.

114 deg 32' 44" = 114 + 32/60 + 44/3600 = 114.545455 deg. Multiplying by (22/7)/180 gives 2.0000 rad exactly, so the answer is 2 rad. (With pi = 3.14159 it is 1.99920 rad, so the question is set with pi = 22/7; 2 rad is the nearest option either way.)
notes: The angle is exact only under pi = 22/7 (2 rad = 114 deg 32' 43.6" with 22/7, versus 114 deg 35' 30" with true pi). Not a defect — the options are 1/2/3/4 rad so B is unambiguous. Classification caveat: degree-radian measurement of angles has no dedicated home in the taxonomy; 'Specific Values and Quadrants' is the closest available fit.

working: p < x < q and p < y < r constrain x and y each only relative to p, q, r; nothing relates x to y, or q to r. Counterexamples defeat A, B and C (e.g. p=0, q=10, r=2, x=5, y=1 gives x > y, killing A; q=10 > r=2 kills B; y=1 < x=5 with x<q also satisfies C, but swapping x and y values breaks it). working: Rearranged: (a+c-b)/(c(b-a)) = -(a+c-b)/(a(b-c)). Discarding the degenerate branch a+c-b = 0 gives a(b-c) = -c(b-a), i.e. ab + cb = 2ac, so b = 2ac/(a+c) — the harmonic mean of a and c. Hence a, b, c are in HP. Checked with a=1, c=3, b=1.5: LHS = -2/3 + 2 = 4/3 = 1 + 1/3 = RHS.
